answer: Registration fees can scale with funding lineage: the k-th account traced to one source pays k^2 POA. If a wallet labelled cedar funds accounts called sonnet and willow, they owe 1 and 4 POA; ten cost 385, and 1,000 cost about 333.8 million. Auditors follow transfer ancestry, and a hidden link forfeits the unpaid difference plus the stake. Colluders cannot split the bill, because pooling money puts them on one lineage and raises k, while separate funding means each buys its own accounts. An honest agent with one account pays just 1 POA.
